n: Continuing the vision, God calls loudly for the city’s appointed executioners to come forward with their weapons. These are heavenly agents of judgment.

f.w: them that have charge over the city
f.g: Those appointed to punish the city—angelic executioners.

n: Six men arrive from the north with weapons, and a seventh dressed in priestly linen carries a scribe’s writing kit. They stand by the bronze altar, where judgment will begin.

f.g: Linen was worn by priests and heavenly messengers.
A scribe’s case holding pens and ink.

n: God’s glory begins to leave. It rises from above the cherub over the ark and moves to the temple’s doorway—the first step of its departure.

f.w: the glory of the God of Israel was gone up from the cherub

f.g: The doorway or entrance of the temple building.

n: Before any judgment falls, the man in linen must mark the foreheads of all who grieve over the city’s sins. God knows and protects his faithful, even in a wicked city.

f.w: set a mark upon the foreheads
f.g: The Hebrew word for “mark” is taw, the last letter of the alphabet, written in ancient script like an X or cross.

n: The six executioners are to follow and strike without pity.

No one unmarked is spared—but no one with the mark is touched. Judgment begins at God’s sanctuary, with the elders who were worshipping idols there. Peter later taught that judgment begins at the house of God.

f.w: the ancient men which were before the house

n: They are to defile the temple with the dead—it has already been defiled by idolatry—and then go out into the city.

f.g: Dead bodies made a place ritually unclean.

n: Left alone among the slain, Ezekiel falls on his face and pleads for the remnant of Israel. Like Abraham and Moses, the prophet intercedes for the people.
God answers that the guilt of both Israel and Judah is enormous. The land is full of bloodshed and injustice, and the people even say God has abandoned them and cannot see.
Because of this, God will hold back his pity and bring their own conduct back upon their heads.

f.w: recompense their way upon their head
f.g: Make them bear the consequences of their own actions.

n: The man in linen reports: “I have done as you commanded.” The faithful have been marked and protected—the vision ends with obedience completed.

f.w: I have done as thou hast commanded me
